convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? I have been lying about my age — I'm younger than I look."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Nino shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"I needed someone to know — just one person. Thank you for being that person."
"The cistern's nearly dry — 0 liters left. Haul the creek with me at dawn? Two buckets each, there and back."
"0 liters. That's today's drinking water, and then we're boiling creek water and hoping. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
Move next to your partner, on the same side of the Haven door.
"Right. Done. Don't look so relieved."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? At night I cry quietly so no one hears."
"Thank you. I needed someone to know, and now someone does. Please keep it there. Be kind to yourself, okay?"
"What's your first memory? Like, ever. The earliest thing."
"Take your time."
"Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started."
They nod, slow. "Okay. Thank you for telling me. That couldn't have been easy to say."
"Still on that question. No pressure, though."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Cormac always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"...Hi. Sorry. I'm not good at the talking-to-strangers part."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Oh. Okay. That's... that's fine, then."
"The way I read it — Strangers are just people you haven't disappointed yet. That's what my mother said. Terrible advice, but it got me through parties."
"It rewards action, not thought. You learn that fast when you're actually out there instead of theorizing about it."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on the big questions."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
Sofia: "Can I ask you something? ... I want us to stick together. Properly. Watch each other's backs."
"Stick together, then." They look steadier already.

"Never mind the pantry run — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. The cistern's nearly dry — 0 liters left. I need someone to haul water with me at first light. Two of us, half the trips. Will you come?"
"Do the math with me: 0 liters, 10 people. That's not tomorrow's water. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Never mind. You had something to say?"
"I dreamed Cormac was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About the creek water run — the need hasn't gone anywhere. I'm still asking."
"I still need help with the creek water run."
Stand beside your partner first — same side of the Haven door — then help.
"Forget it — go on, I'm listening."
"Cormac owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"I've got things to do. People to avoid. You know."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
Niamh: "You. Yeah, you. What do you make of this?"
"Take your time."
Something in them stays shut, for now.
"Still on that question."
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Since Cormac died... I keep expecting to see Cormac at the fire. Stupid."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Niamh grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Niamh is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"I wake before anyone else. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
Someone out there knows something. I just have to find the right someone.
"Blood first. Then the family you choose. I'm building the second kind here, too."
"I'd trade every comfortable day left in my life for one hour with them."
"Still on wanting to find their family."
They let that thread drop — for now.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Niamh nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Enough about what I'm chasing. What did you want?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "They took Niamh — The Blood Tithe, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
You show them Mayapple — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here?"
"That's the good stuff. Quiet generosity. It's holding this whole thing together."
"Sure — Someone saved me the last of the stew once. Didn't say anything, just put the bowl down and walked off. I think about that bowl more than I think about the monsters."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on the kindest thing someone's done for you."
"I don't do parties. ...It's not you. It's the party."
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"I'm not from Denver. I'm from Columbus, Ohio. Someone I love needed the lie more than I needed the truth."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Jamie rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"We went over this," Jamie says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"See you around."

"We never did finish talking about that water haul — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'Do the math with me: 0 liters, 10 people. That's not tomorrow's water. We walk together and each carry two…'"
"My cut needs a second pair of hands. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."

"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The Blood Tithe. They just... took Niamh. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Same as always: we endure."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"I should go. Before I overthink this conversation too."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk? Have you seen anyone on the roads? Anyone at all? I'm asking everyone."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"We're down to 0 liters of clean water. Haul the creek with me at dawn? Two buckets each, there and back."
"I checked the cistern three times hoping I misread it. 0 liters. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."

"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that water haul."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You told me about people sharing food they couldn't spare. Quiet. No performance. Seen it again since?"

"0 liters. That's today's drinking water, and then we're boiling creek water and hoping. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Have you felt it? Like the air before a storm, but — bigger. Something's on its way."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
You show them Dandelion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Alright, duty calls. This was a good pause."

"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I stole from someone who trusted me. I think about it every day."
Desmond has an edge today — something curdled.
Their whole posture softens around you.
"Mugwort — crush the leaf, smell it, taste the stem. That's how you know it."
"This one is Jujube. Look at the leaf, feel the stem, breathe it in. It'll stick."
"Thank you for hearing it. I needed someone to know — and I needed it to stop with you."

"Do the math with me: 0 liters, 9 people. That's not tomorrow's water. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."

"It's nothing, really. What were you saying?"
"Hannah killed the things that come at night. I did too. That's a small club, and it's smaller now."
"About what they confided — yeah, we never did get back to that."
"I still need help with the creek water run."
"I should go. You know where to find me."

"...Think about it? I'll be around."

"The fire feels smaller without Hannah. The rest of us will have to be bigger."

"I pace while thinking for Hannah, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."

"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."

"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."

"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"

"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."

"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."

"Alright — I should get back to it."

"I don't have the words for all of it. But thank you for asking."

"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "My well's dry on that one. Ask me tomorrow — maybe I'll have dreamed something."
The moment passes without landing. Not yet.
"Right. I get it." A beat — and then the subject is closed. For today, anyway.
"Still on that water haul."

"Roles. Not ranks — promises."

"Same time tomorrow, maybe."

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Cormac Nolan is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Cormac is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d41: Emberhold watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer. (Trust -8.)
d41: 🕯️ Cormac Nolan is dead — the arena. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Cormac kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Cormac's gone." Nino looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Cormac." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Hannah blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.

d41: ★ The record corrects itself: this was never Piquiarana — it's Common Plantain. A person, maybe 40s taught you wrong (their own memory). (The Codex marks the disagreement. You can call them out in conversation.)
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Camp Cooking (Level 1). Cooking uses half the water, +10% kcal. Once per day: add a Secret Ingredient (a random inventory item) — 50% delicious (+morale), 50% educational.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Boiling Water (Level 1). Rolling boil for 1 minute kills most pathogens. The simplest safe water.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Food Preservation (Level 1). Salt, smoke, dry. The big three. Salt draws water out; bacteria can't live without it.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Field Dressing (Level 1). Break down game fast and clean. Less waste, more meat, usable parts.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: The Forager’s Eye (Level 1). You walk slower and see more. Food was always there; now you notice it.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Cormac Nolan, 41 days. The mantle passes to Hannah Kim.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Hannah Kim, 28 — a Chef. Her hands know different work now: Iron Stomach, Green Thumb, Literally, Purify, Dowsing.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Cormac — and Cormac is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Jamie, Niamh, Dieter and 6 more speak for Hannah — "Cormac trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Hannah before the Codex did — her name already carried weight here.
